Hi Sara / Tony -

Thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap and next steps on the encryption / data handling topics we covered: 

Summary (what we covered)
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ between clients and Redwood endpoints; optional mTLS for private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for model artifacts and stored caches.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): Redwood supports BYOK via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for hosted Dedicated and Private deployments. HSM-backed keys are supported where the cloud provider exposes them (e.g., AWS CloudHSM-backed KMS).
- Private deployments: for full HSM on-prem scenarios we can run the control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package to integrate with your HSM.
- Logging & retention: audit logs (access, admin ops) available with configurable retention; token-level logs can be limited for PII-sensitive workloads.

Action items / next steps
1) Security workshop: propose 60-90 minute session with your security/infra team to walk architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and KMS integration patterns. (Owner: Marissa)
2) Provide a short pre-read that outlines tech options + data flow and a matrix of tradeoffs (attached: redwood-kms-arch.png, soc2-security-brief.pdf). (Owner: Marissa)
3) Legal/procurement: Tony, you mentioned a requirement for a KMS addendum in the MSA if we will use CMKs. We can surface standard language and an optional SOW. (Owner: Tony/Acme)
4) Schedule: please share availability for the workshop next week.

If helpful I can include our solutions engineer (Priyom) and SE lead (Nikhil) on the workshop - they can deep-dive on key rotation, key wrapping, and HSM support.

Thanks,

4) Retention: our legal team requires retention of system logs for 7 years for specific endpoints; is that configurable and would it apply to token-level logs (we prefer token logs to be purged or masked by default)?

Hi Sara - great questions. Short answers below; I attached a 2-page pre-read (kms-options.pdf) that lays these out with diagrams and recommended next steps. More detail available in the workshop.

1) BYOK / key access model
- Default BYOK flow: customer retains key material in their KMS. Redwood holds only a reference (key ARN / key id) and uses the cloud KMS APIs to perform cryptographic operations or to unwrap keys. We do not persist plaintext key material in our control plane. For Dedicated and hosted modes, the KMS operations happen over secure API calls and keys remain under your KMS policy scope.
- For Private / on-prem deployments we can integrate directly with your HSM over a secure channel so Redwood has zero access to key material.

2) HSM-backed keys
- Supported. For AWS: we support KMS keys backed by CloudHSM (i.e., AWS KMS keys with custom key material). You will need to ensure key policy allows the Redwood service principal to use Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey (we provide a minimal policy snippet).
- For GCP/Azure we support equivalent provider-managed HSMs (Cloud HSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) where their KMS exposes key usage APIs. Our SEs will review required IAM/policy changes during the workshop.

3) Region scoping / data residency
- KMS: you can provision keys in the region of your choice; Redwood will call the regional KMS endpoints for key ops so key material stays in-region. For hosted Dedicated, we recommend selecting a dedicated region/cluster for EU workloads.
- Logs: audit logs are stored in region-bound stores (configurable per-account for Dedicated/Private). For hosted multi-region setups we can enable regional log partitioning.

4) Retention and token-level logs
- Retention windows are configurable in the Console for audit logs and request logs. Token-level logs (full inputs/outputs) are disabled-by-default for PII-sensitive customers and can be configured to mask/purge after a configurable window (including immediate purge). We can include a clause in the agreement stating default masking for PII-sensitive endpoints.

- Tony / Acme: if you can share the standard KMS addendum language ahead of time we can align and surface any Redwood template changes prior to the workshop.

If that all looks good I’ll get calendar invites out.
